pr_title: X509_dup: fix copying of libctx and propq using new ASN1_OP_DUP_POST cb operation
pr_body:
This fixes #12680.

Unfortunately the arg types of the generic ASN.1 callback function:
```
typedef int ASN1_aux_cb(int operation, ASN1_VALUE **in, const ASN1_ITEM *it,
                        void *exarg);
```
are not really adequate here, so I had to use pretty ugly casts, but it works.
pr_comments:
Likely more `X509` fields could/should be copied,
and the new `ASN1_OP_DUP_*` could be of help also for other `_dup` implementations,
but that would be beyond the scope of this quick fix.
@levitte, can you meanwhile approve this (subject to test passing, which seem to get delayed more than usual today)?

Starting to see these a bit in appveyor
Can't spawn "cmd.exe": No such file or directory at ..\..\util\wrap.pl line 31.
Does anyone know if something new is causing this?
travis also got an error

> travis also got an error

Sigh, now some strange errors and hanging behavior shows up.
It looks like I'll need some more time to investigate on this, which I do not have today since I'm traveling...
Re cmd.exe, I haven't seen that before. I'll check later today

The appveyor error looks suspicious..
ASN1_item_dup:aux error:..\crypto\asn1\a_dup.c:78:

> The appveyor error looks suspicious..
> ASN1_item_dup:aux error:..\crypto\asn1\a_dup.c:78:

Thx for pointing out this issue. I was already aware of it but so far did not have the time to look at it.

This error is pretty strange because it does not happen with any Travis configuration 
any only with one AppVeyor configuration, where the only difference appears to be 
`VC-WIN32 no-asm --strict-warnings` vs. `VC-WIN64A-masm`.

I cannot reproduce this on my Linux system.
In an attempt to get a little more date I've pushed a commit with a couple of exploratory changes.

I'm giving up on a pretty weird issue that makes various tests fail due to the following errors:
```
74080000:error::asn1 encoding routines:asn1_item_embed_d2i:illegal options on item template:..\crypto\asn1\tasn_dec.c:178:Type=X509_NAME_INTERNAL
74080000:error::asn1 encoding routines:ASN1_item_dup:aux error:..\crypto\asn1\a_dup.c:83:Type=X509_NAME
```
This happens only for one AppVeyor build (Windows, Environment: VSVER=15; Configuration: shared; Platform: x86).
So I cannot reproduce this locally on my Linux system.

For whatever reason, there is an ASN.1 error for `X509_NAME_INTERNAL`
and then `asn1_cb` is non-NULL for `X509_NAME` and its invocation fails.

I've added a workaround for the `X509_NAME` case, which simply prevents invoking the callback(which is not needed there anyway).

@levitte, is this acceptable for now?
Or does anyone have a better solution?

For the record, the weird failures that show for Visual Studio 15 shared x86 builds (only) can be seen in
https://ci.appveyor.com/project/openssl/openssl/builds/34815697/job/f2uy0j05wk49vmtc?fullLog=true
Ping @levitte
The failure really looks suspicious. Could there be some problem/memory corruption or something that manifests on 32bit only?

> The failure really looks suspicious. Could there be some problem/memory corruption or something that manifests on 32bit only?

Thanks @t8m for having a look at that.

If it is due to some so far unnoticed memory corruption then this normally would lead to a crash.
Yet the `aux->asn1_cb`, which should be `NULL` for `X509_NAME`, appears to be a valid function pointer, 
and I have no clue which code might be responsible for setting this pointer to anything non-NULL.
At least apparently this does not happen for Linux and any other type of Windows build. 

The problem very likely is a weird consequence of 
`74080000:error::asn1 encoding routines:asn1_item_embed_d2i:illegal options on item template:..\crypto\asn1\tasn_dec.c:178:Type=X509_NAME_INTERNAL`
and also there I don't understand why this surfaces only for that specific type of build.
@levitte or @mattcaswell - are you happy with this PR?
Just rebased this in order to solve an alleged merge conflict with asn1t.h.
As this is bug fix imo this can go in after beta. Better than having the uncovered issue hidden.

> As this is bug fix imo this can go in after beta. Better than having the uncovered issue hidden.

Agreed. This is a bug fix, so I'm removing the beta 1 milestone.

> Agreed. This is a bug fix, so I'm removing the beta 1 milestone.

Err no..

The public function X509_dup_with_libctx() is removed in this PR. I dont consider that bit to be a bug fix.

> > Agreed. This is a bug fix, so I'm removing the beta 1 milestone.
> 
> Err no..
> 
> The public function X509_dup_with_libctx() is removed in this PR. I dont consider that bit to be a bug fix.

No, just a workaround function of that name used in some tests is removed.
This PR fixes insufficient behavior of `X509_dup`.
See the title and intro text of this PR.

It is a bug fix (which currently contains another workaround for some other bug).

> The public function X509_dup_with_libctx() is removed in this PR.

Its not a public function. Its entirely internal to the tests.
I've rebased this to solve (trivial) merge conflicts.
This PR is in a state where it requires action by @openssl/otc but the last update was 30 days ago

Thanks @FdaSilvaYY for the analysis of the issue. So basically the `it->funcs` should be used as `ASN1_AUX` structure pointer only if `it->itype != ASN1_ITYPE_EXTERN && it->itype != ASN1_ITYPE_PRIMITIVE`
Or better make the condition the other way around - i.e. only do it for ASN1_ITYPE_SEQUENCE, ASN1_ITYPE_NDEF_SEQUENCE, and ASN1_ITYPE_CHOICE.

Thanks a lot @FdaSilvaYY for point out this:
> @DDvO I dig and get the crash reason :
> 
> you add this line in your PR :
> `const ASN1_AUX *aux = it->funcs;`
>
> But for the `X509_NAME` type, its respective void* it->funcs is not pointing to an expected `X509_AUX` object,
> 
> It is pointing to a structure named `x509_name_ff`,

Indeed for `X509_NAME` the `it->funcs` field has a different type, namely `ASN1_EXTERN_FUNCS`!

BTW, it is unfortunate that the `funcs` field of `ASN1_ITEM` has the entirely generic pointer type `void *` 
and that for most ASN.1 types its name `funcs` and comment `/* functions that handle this type */` is misleading -
only for `ASN1_ITYPE_PRIMITIVE` and `ASN1_ITYPE_EXTERN` (the `X509_NAME` case) this contains more or less function pointers,
while for everything else the field is either `NULL` or a pointer to an `ASN1_AUX` structure, which contains much more than a collection of function pointers.

@t8m wrote:

> So basically the `it->funcs` should be used as `ASN1_AUX` structure pointer only if 
`it->itype != ASN1_ITYPE_EXTERN && it->itype != ASN1_ITYPE_PRIMITIVE`

> Or better make the condition the other way around - i.e. only do it for 
`ASN1_ITYPE_SEQUENCE`, `ASN1_ITYPE_NDEF_SEQUENCE`, and `ASN1_ITYPE_CHOICE`.

How is the situation for the remaining possibility, namely `ASN1_ITYPE_MSTRING` ?
Looks like this is a special case of `ASN1_ITYPE_PRIMITIVE`.
@t8m, I've just implemented your latest solution hint.

Moreover, I've added a commit on `asn1t.h`:

Improve documentation of `ASN1_ITYPE_..` and add TODO on `funcs` field, which 
hopefully helps preventing in the future tricky bugs like the one in this PR, which was very hard to find.
Also move the `#define`s for the `ASN1_ITYPE_..` before their first use.

> IMO this is almost mergeable - I have just one comment.

Pleased to hear. Can you now approve with the new wording of the comments on the 'funcs' field?
```
    const void *funcs;          /* further data and type-specific functions */
    /* funcs can be ASN1_PRIMITIVE_FUNCS*, ASN1_EXTERN_FUNCS*, or ASN1_AUX* */
```
We may want to put a hold on approving some of these things that are no longer being tested by travis :)

> We may want to put a hold on approving some of these things that are no longer being tested by travis :)

Well, the hold was on merging, not on approving :smile:

(And in this special case the problem just corrected yesterday was detected by AppVeyor only).
@DDvO can you please rebase to pick-up the GitHub CI?

> @DDvO can you please rebase to pick-up the GitHub CI?

Sure, done.
This pull request is ready to merge

Finally, merged.
Thanks @slontis, @FdaSilvaYY, @levitte, and @t8m.

issue_context.title: X509_dup() does not copy libctx (and likely neither any other non-ASN.1 fields)
issue_context.body:
One would expect that `X509_dup()` copies all fields, but at least for `libctx` this is not the case,
likely because it is implemented solely by a generic ASN.1 structure copying function 
and this does not copy other other fields of `x509_st`.

See also https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/11808#discussion_r471092440 and https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/11808#discussion_r472908941.
comments: That is not good.. I assume this is not used very often then.. libctx needs to be copied.
I believe the callback should take care of that. There should be a callback operator for duplication...
I cannot find any callback for `dup`, at least not in `crypto/asn1/a_dup.c`.

Yup, I found that too...  so I'd suggest adding a duplication callback operation...  ASN1_OP_DUP_PRE and ASN1_OP_DUP_POST, say?

_PRE would be called on the source object, and _POST would be called on the destination object, *with the source object as last argument*.  That way, the callback can be used to prepare the source for duplication (if ever needed), and to copy extra stuff from the source to the destination.

Does that sound workable?  Are you willing to do it, @DDvO?  I've got my hands full already, so would rather not.
I can give it a try tonight...

The fix is in #12687.
This turned out to be doable pretty quickly because the callback function basically was already there.

review_comments:
Interesting thought -
I do not see how `x509_cb` could be called in any other context than for pointers of type `X509 *`, but who knows.
So if you can debug this on such an environment, would be great in particular to obtain a backtrace that leads to the situation currently excluded by the workaround
```
#ifdef OPENSSL_SYS_WINDOWS
    /*
     * Workaround for following issue with Windows VS 15 shared x86 builds:
     * 74080000:error::asn1 encoding routines:asn1_item_embed_d2i:illegal options on item template:..\crypto\asn1\tasn_dec.c:178:Type=X509_NAME_INTERNAL
     * 74080000:error::asn1 encoding routines:ASN1_item_dup:aux error:..\crypto\asn1\a_dup.c:83:Type=X509_NAME
    */
    if (asn1_cb != NULL && strcmp(it->sname, "X509_NAME") == 0)
        asn1_cb = NULL;
#endif
```
So please replace the `#ifdef OPENSSL_SYS_WINDOWS` e.g. by `#if 1` and set breakpoint on `asn1_cb = NULL;`
and then let's analyze how execution arrived there.
Drive by comment: I note that X509_new_with_libctx() doesn't "dup" the propq, and hence you don't here either. We probably should.
I will do this once this PR is merged..
Reported as #13486 so we do not forget.
